text: Drake Maye faces a formidable test in Week 2 as the Patriots seek their first win of the season against a rolling Steelers squad, with the young quarterback tasked with balancing patience and aggression against Pittsburgh's daunting defense in Sunday's 1 PM ET home opener at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots' offensive chess match against the Steelers will play out without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III (downgraded to out), though the injury news isn't all bad—TreVeyon Henderson says he's "ready to go" after missing the opener with an ankle injury, and punter Mitch Wishnowsky has been elevated from the practice squad for the week. The matchup comes with added poignancy as Stephon Gilmore, the two-time All-Pro and 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year who spent much of his Hall of Fame career in New England, signed a one-day contract Friday to retire as a Patriot, a fitting bookend to Bill Belichick's 24-year tenure appreciating the elite defense of the league's best.
